newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia changes bank reserve requirements May 1.
newsitem.headline: Russia changes bank reserve requirements May 1.

text.p: The Russian central bank decided on Friday it was cutting banks' reserve requirements for rouble deposits and raising requirements on foreign currency deposits from May 1, a spokesman said.
He declined to comment further on the move, agreed at a meeting of the bank's policy-making board of directors.

But bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said in December the central bank intended to eliminate gradually the difference between reserve requirements on rouble and currency deposits as part of its policy of de-dollarising the Russian economy.
Reserve requirements for rouble sight deposits and time deposits up to 30 days fall to 14 percent from 16 percent.
Reserve requirements for rouble time deposits from 31 to 90 days fall to 11 from 13 percent. Requirements for rouble time deposits longer than 91 days fall to eight from 10 percent.
Reserve requirements on all maturities of currency deposits rise to six from five percent.
